paper_metadata.title: Quantum-Assisted Machine Learning for Enhanced Fraud Detection in Cybersecurity

experiments.description: Quantum Support Vector Classifier for credit card fraud detection using a Pauli feature map and quantum kernel on a balanced subset of the European credit card fraud dataset.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical credit card transaction features are mapped into quantum states using a Pauli feature map and evaluated with a quantum kernel.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of fraudulent vs. legitimate transactions.

problem_instance.description: Fraud detection on credit card transactions from European cardholders in September 2013, using a balanced training subset.

dataset_specification.description: European cardholder transactions from September 2013; 32 attributes including Time and Amount; Class is binary target; 492 fraud cases out of 284,807 total transactions; class imbalance addressed by randomly sampling 300 non-fraud transactions to match fraud count; 75% training and 25% testing split; features normalized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1; PCA applied; Min-Max scaling to [0, 4].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Correlation coefficients computed for each feature against Class; missing data removed; balanced subset created by random sampling of 300 non-fraud transactions; normalized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1; PCA used for dimensionality reduction; Min-Max scaling to [0, 4].
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Performance evaluated on a 75/25 train-test split using accuracy, precision, and recall.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Correlation analysis, missing-data removal, class balancing by random undersampling, normalization, PCA, and Min-Max scaling.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classification metrics computed from predictions: accuracy, precision, recall.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit speedup or runtime comparison was reported.
